fact: Shega reports that Ethiopia's first personal data protection proclamation took effect on publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette, a year before the article, though implementation has been slow (as_of is the article's published date; the document gives no commencement date).

The Ethiopian Communications Authority, whose mandate was extended from telecom regulation to data protection, is described as enforcing the law, with its Director General Balcha Reba saying data processors and collectors now need the Authority's permission and that staffing and technical capacity are being expanded (date is the article's published date).

Shega reports that delays in issuing directives have slowed implementation and that four directives are still expected to be approved in the coming months, so none of them is yet in force (date is the article's published date).

The ECA Director General told Shega the Authority had received about 10 requests to transfer data abroad and had approved them as a temporary measure, and officials previewed a forthcoming registration portal for data controllers and processors at a workshop co-hosted with Huawei; the article records no sanction or published count of decisions, noting that as of March 2025 no ECA enforcement actions or guidelines had been publicized.

At a workshop co-hosted with Huawei in the week before 15 November 2025, ECA officials previewed a digital portal for controller and processor registration and said four directives would be approved in the coming months, while the article calls the overall regime more aspirational than fully realised.

The overview states that Proclamation No. 1321/2024, Ethiopia's first comprehensive personal data protection law, was approved on 4 April 2024 and published in the Federal Negarit Gazette on 24 July 2024; it gives no commencement date.
The overview states that the proclamation designates the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulator; it does not say the Authority is acting under the law.

Addis Fortune reports that Ethiopia's first personal data protection proclamation, three years in the making, was put before Parliament's Standing Committee on Human Resource Development, Employment & Technology Affairs the week before 13 January 2024.
UNESCO's profile lists the Personal Data Protection Proclamation among the instruments shaping Ethiopia's legal framework.
FaydaVerse says its OTP verification adheres to the Personal Data Protection Act.
Digital Policy Alert states that Ethiopia implemented the Personal Data Protection Proclamation in July 2024.
Digital Policy Alert states that the Ethiopian Communications Authority oversees compliance with the Proclamation and must be consulted on high-risk processing.
Digital Policy Alert states there are currently no public, official sources on enforcement action or guidelines by the Ethiopian Communications Authority.
Birr Metrics refers to Ethiopia's Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 as mandating domestic storage of data collected in the country, with strict conditions on cross-border transfer.
Xalam Analytics describes the Personal Data Protection Proclamation of 2024 as requiring companies to host citizen data in Ethiopia, with strict regulation of cross-border transfers.

Ethiopian News Agency reports that the Ethiopian Communications Authority, whose Director General Balcha Reba spoke, acts under its legal mandate on personal data protection and held a stakeholder consultation on the Proclamation's implementation.
Ethiopian News Agency reports on 13 May 2026 that the Communications Authority held a consultation on the implementation and application of Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321/2016 EC.

The Communications Authority's Director General said a portal has been prepared for individuals to report personal-data breaches to the regulator, and the Authority held a stakeholder consultation on implementation, with no decision stated.

The law firm Haymanot & Advocates describes Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 as providing a comprehensive legal framework for collecting, processing, storing and transferring personal data, with which banks must comply.
